stem: Out of 200 students in a school, 120 study Mathematics, 90 study Science, and 40 study neither. Using a Venn diagram approach, find the number of students who study both Mathematics and Science.

per_option_rationale.rationale: n(M union S) = 200 - 40 = 160. By inclusion-exclusion: 160 = 120 + 90 - n(both), so n(both) = 210 - 160 = 50.
This comes from 120 + 90 - 200 = 10, subtracting the total instead of the union count, a slip in applying the formula.
This comes from 200 - 40 - 120 - 90 + 60 = 10... or from (120+90)/4 = 52.5 rounded to 30, a rough estimation error.
This comes from using n(neither) = 40 to write n(both) = 120 + 90 - 200 + 40 + 20 = 70, confusing neither with the intersection in the formula.

explanation: n(M union S) = n(total) - n(neither) = 200 - 40 = 160. By inclusion-exclusion: n(M union S) = n(M) + n(S) - n(M intersect S). So 160 = 120 + 90 - n(both), giving n(both) = 210 - 160 = 50.

explanation_sections.punchline: The neither count tells you n(union) = 160, then inclusion-exclusion back-solves for the intersection.
explanation_sections.approach: Step 1: n(union) = n(U) - n(neither) = 200 - 40 = 160. Step 2: inclusion-exclusion n(M intersect S) = n(M) + n(S) - n(union) = 120 + 90 - 160 = 50.
explanation_sections.lesson: When neither is given, compute n(union) first; then the intersection follows from inclusion-exclusion.
explanation_sections.timing: 60 s. The trap is subtracting n(U) instead of n(union) in the inclusion-exclusion step.
